items.t: Charging unit (ICCU) failure and loss of drive power (recall)
12-volt battery goes flat and the car won't wake up
items.job: Test the 12-volt battery and charging unit, then replace the 12-volt battery
items.note: Parts: genuine Hyundai 12-volt battery 37110-P1610, $119 online to $153 list. Labor based on YourMechanic's Ioniq 5 (same E-GMP platform) battery job: $248 parts + $140 labor. If the ICCU charging unit is the cause, the recall covers that repair.

items.t: Reduction gear bolts may be loose (recall)
Charging port door panel can fall off (recall)
Front seat belt anchors may detach (recall)
'Power is limited' warning with turtle light
items.job: Diagnose power-limited warning per Hyundai bulletin
items.note: Drive motor parts are normally covered by Hyundai's EV warranty.

items.t: Home Level 2 charging slows down or charge port gets hot
items.job: Inspect AC charging inlet and update charging software
items.note: Replacing the charging inlet costs more and should be covered under warranty.

items.t: Charging port insulation caps missing or damaged
Brake lights and i-Pedal behave oddly during regenerative braking
Doors don't unlock as you walk up
items.job: Smart Approach Unlock repair per bulletin

items.t: Power trunk lid doesn't latch fully
items.job: Power trunk latch repair per bulletin
